Freshness.description:
How current one source is, from two sides that must never be confused (Austin, 2026-10-24).

(a) Source side -- ``late_to_refresh``: the publisher (hospital, insurer, agency, clinic) is
    past its own deadline. Shown to users as "late to refresh"; the data is still shown.
(b) Our side -- ``stale_on_our_side``: OUR last successful fetch/check is older than our own
    schedule. That is our fault, never the publisher's; the UI and /our-data say so.

Rule: we only call a publisher late when our own check is current. If we are stale we do not
know whether they published since, so ``late_to_refresh`` must be False.
Build these with ``Freshness.compute`` so every producer applies the same cadences.

expected_by.description: (a) When the publisher owed a newer version under source_rule. None = no deadline.
expected_by.title: Expected By

fetched_at.description: (b) our last successful fetch / check of this source
fetched_at.title: Fetched At

last_updated.description: (a) The source's own date: file last_updated_on, fee schedule effective date, date printed on a clinic page. None = the source states no date.
last_updated.title: Last Updated

late_to_refresh.description: (a) publisher past its deadline (and our check is current)
late_to_refresh.title: Late To Refresh

our_refresh_due.description: (b) when our next fetch/check was due under our_rule. None = no newer release known.
our_refresh_due.title: Our Refresh Due

stale_on_our_side.description: (b) we are behind our own schedule
stale_on_our_side.title: Stale On Our Side

Freshness.title: Freshness
